messages.content:
Honestly, I’m frustrated and exhausted by this submission experience.

My notebook runs for 8.3 hours on the public practice games and scores 46.90. When submitted for competition evaluation, it finishes in less than an hour with 0.00.

I understand that the hidden games are different. I’m not expecting the same score. But the dramatically shorter runtime makes me question whether the agent even ran as intended. So I’m left with no explanation beyond “0.00.” Did initialization fail? Did the agent execute any actions? Did it terminate early? Or did it genuinely play and solve nothing?

With limited submission attempts and days left, repeatedly submitting speculative fixes is incredibly discouraging. I’m not asking for hidden game details, just enough execution diagnostics to distinguish an actual performance failure from a broken run. Even a minimal report would help:

  • Did the model server and agent initialize?
  • How many games started and actions executed?
  • What was the actual execution duration?
  • Why did the run stop?

Has anyone encountered this and found a concrete cause? Is there a supported way to debug it without burning another submission blindly?

messages.content:
I suspect this may be on the Kaggle side.

Others are reporting similar problems here: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/arc-prize-2026-arc-agi-3/discussion/751598

Our checkpoint read pass went from about 5 minutes to 35, with the same model versions, container and launcher.

We tested plain file reads before importing PyTorch or allocating model memory and they were already slow. On one RTX PRO 6000 worker, 16 readers managed about 119 MiB/s, with NFS read requests taking 120 ms on average. A fresh worker with the same configuration gave about 291 MiB/s and 49 ms.

There was almost no local RPC queueing, and no NFS retransmissions or errors were recorded. We cleared the local file cache between tests, although we couldn’t control the server-side cache.

Adding more readers didn’t help much: going from 16 to 64 improved average throughput over full shards by only about 4%.

That seems to narrow it down to the remote storage read path, though we can’t tell from these measurements whether the delay is in the network or the storage backend.

Could someone at Kaggle check for contention or bandwidth limits on the model mounts? The difference between otherwise similarly configured workers might also be worth looking into.

replies.content:
The scorecard can expire after 15 minutes if there’s no game action while the model loads. Increasing the model startup timeout alone won’t prevent that.

A proposed workaround is to send a counted RESET every 5 minutes until the server is ready. Downsides are extra actions on that game and loading time eating into the 9hr budget. The per-game timeout also needs enough headroom.

We’ve tested the mechanism locally, but haven’t validated a complete submission with it yet.

replies.content:
Quick update: yesterday’s submission with the ‘startup guard’ completed successfully and posted a score within the expected range. Startup took about 46 minutes.

The guard sends a RESET every five minutes while waiting for the model server, then stops once it’s ready. As mentioned, startup eats into the 9hr budget (around 30 minutes less playing time available now) and RESETs count towards the action total, so this doesn’t remove the cost of the slow loading.
